title: The Kings' Gate
journal: Never-Writes-Twice says the marked tower is one of the drowned spires off Lilmoth, and the divers of Bell Station will know which. This is the order's hunt; my own errand to Fort Chalkmoth may wait or come first. I'm to ask the steward of Bell Station, on an islet east of Lilmoth, which tower the stone marks.
objectives: Ask the steward of Bell Station which tower the marker stone shows. (marker: Meer-Tasi, Sees-Below)

plan.going: The order's hunt goes on; the marker stone's tower is a drowned spire off Lilmoth. My own errand to Fort Chalkmoth is open beside it.
plan.next: Ask the steward of Bell Station which tower it is.
plan.ways: Either order with Fort Chalkmoth; one way here, a question.

answers: I am hunting for the location of a gate tied to the Kings Marker Stone I recovered from the Stormwidow. Never-Writes-Twice in Helstrom says the marked tower is one of the drowned spires off Lilmoth. The Unbound are also after this, and the Collector Vanin is digging ahead of us.
Ask the steward of Bell Station, an islet east of Lilmoth, which tower the stone marks. The quest markers are on Meer-Tasi and Sees-Below.
I can talk to Meer-Tasi or Sees-Below, and I could go to Fort Chalkmoth first for my own errand. I favour sneaking.
I do not know who Meer-Tasi and Sees-Below are or which is the steward. I also do not know what moans in the Fort Chalkmoth cellar or what the Kings Gate is. I can find out by talking to people.

title: The Kings' Gate
journal: The steward, Meer-Tasi, knew the cut tower at once: Teku-Sul Spire, the drowned tower nearest Lilmoth, whose great gate her divers have never forced. The dive is long. I need a Hist's blessing, a spell or potion of waterbreathing (she sells them) or an enchantment, unless I am Argonian; inside the tower there is air. I'm to dive to Teku-Sul and find the great gate. The drowned priests' attendants walk its east halls; I may fight them or slip past.
objectives: Find the great gate deep in Teku-Sul Spire. (marker: Door to Teku-Sul East Halls, Door to Teku-Sul Halls, Ghost of Sul-Xeeth)

plan.going: The marked tower is Teku-Sul Spire, under the sea; its great gate has never been forced.
plan.next: Dive to Teku-Sul and find the great gate beyond the east halls.
plan.ways: Breathe by a potion (bought or brewed), a blessing, a spell, an enchantment, or being Argonian; fight the attendants, turn them with Restoration, or pass them by stealth.

answers: The stone marks Teku-Sul Spire, the drowned tower nearest Lilmoth. It has a great gate with three empty sockets that nobody has forced, and a priest ghost stands before it.
Dive to Teku-Sul and find the great gate, going through the Halls and East Halls doors. I need waterbreathing first (a potion from Meer-Tasi, or I may breathe water already if I am Argonian).
I can buy waterbreathing potions from Meer-Tasi. Inside I can fight the priests attendants or sneak past them, and I can talk to the ghost of Sul-Xeeth. I could also go to Fort Chalkmoth first.
I do not know what the three sockets take, who Sul-Xeeth was, or what the gate opens. I can ask the ghost and look around inside.

title: The Kings' Gate
journal: Before the great gate in Teku-Sul stands the ghost of a priest of the old kings, Sul-Xeeth. The gate has three empty sockets, one for each seal-stone the last king's priests cut, and only all three open it. One lies in the warden's vault at Blackrose Prison, one in the flooded vaults of Gemin, one in the deepest hall of Vorannuhl. I'm to tell Never-Writes-Twice in Nesh-Deeka's House in Helstrom.
objectives: Tell Never-Writes-Twice in Nesh-Deeka's House, Helstrom, what the ghost said. (marker: Never-Writes-Twice)

plan.going: The gate needs three seal-stones; I know where each lies.

answers: I reached the Kings Gate in Teku-Sul. The ghost of priest Sul-Xeeth says three seal-stones open it, all three needed. They are at Blackrose Prison (warden vault), the flooded vaults of Gemin, and the deepest hall of Vorannuhl. Beyond is the way to the Root where the Hist roots meet and the Eye sits.
Tell Never-Writes-Twice in Nesh-Deeka House, Helstrom what the ghost said.
I can report to her, or begin fetching stones myself, or do my Fort Chalkmoth errand. The drowned attendants here could be fought or avoided.
I do not know what the Eye is, why the Unbound and Vanin want it, or what the Root holds. I could ask Never-Writes-Twice or the ghost.

title: The Kings' Gate
journal: Never-Writes-Twice made me a Reel-Ka, a Warrior of the order, and gave me its heavier armour, three hundred gold and a free bed in every Archwarden fort. Her orders are to take all three seal-stones before the Unbound do. I'm to fetch them from Blackrose Prison, Gemin and Vorannuhl, in any order; all three are marked, Blackrose the least dangerous and Vorannuhl the worst.

plan.going: As at 90; the Chalkmoth errand is done.
plan.next: Take the three stones, in any order (MN14 to MN16).

answers: The Kings Gate quest is complete. I work for the Toh-Reel-Ka and am now a Reel-Ka (Warrior), with the Reel-Ka cuirass and helm, 300 gold and free beds in Archwarden forts. The gate in Teku-Sul Spire needs three seal-stones to open the way to the Root and the Eye of Argonia. The order wants all three before the Unbound get them.
Fetch the stones from Blackrose Prison (warden vault, least dangerous), Gemin (flooded vaults) and Vorannuhl (deepest hall, worst). The markers are on my map.
I can take them in any order and sneak or fight. My Fort Chalkmoth errand is still open, and I still suspect Never-Writes-Twice for dismissing it.

I do not know what the Eye does in the order hands, what Fort Chalkmoth cellar moans are, or what the Unbound and Vanin intend. I could find out at Fort Chalkmoth or the sites themselves. Notes: I never bought waterbreathing potions and did not need them to reach the gate. I carry the Unbound recipe note, 1350 gold or so, and the rapier.
